name: J. Randolph Grymes
role: Company office assistant from New York; later railroad draughtsman
bio: J. Randolph Grymes of New York was engaged by the company in August 1884 to assist in its Medora offices, and in September 1884 received a valuable present from the Baroness. His new house, a substantial building, was finished in November 1884, and in 1885 he took part in a Bad Lands Gun Club shoot, went hunting with Wallace Lozier, and helped mind a store with Keeler. He received votes in the April 1886 Billings County election, and in the fall of 1886 returned to New York, where he was to work as a draughtsman on the Manhattan elevated railroad.
